title: Bill Me Later
summary:
Bill Me Later
The past couple of weeks have been quite tumultuous in the United States financial markets. The wild ride was capped with the fire sale of a cornerstone American investment bank. Bear Stearns was salvaged with a $2 per share offer from JP Morgan giving the bank a total value of less than the current price for two modern VLCCs.

children.title: Can It Happen To Tankers?
children.summary: The question is whether or not the tanker market could experience a similar liquidity crisis. The table below shows the size of the orderbook in the large tanker sectors and the approximate values at current price assessments.

children.title: Orderbook Count
children.summary: Price Assumption Total Orderbook Value 2009 2010 2011+ ($ Million) ($ Billions) VLCC 60 58 40 $150 $29.4 Suezmax 54 41 21 $92 $12.7 Aframax 105 83 30 $76 $21.5 Panamax 46 25 19 $67 $9.2 MR 228 171 97 $52 $37.9 Total 493 378 207 $110.8 The above figure of $110 billion excludes the financing needed for chemical carriers, dry bulk carriers, container ships, LNG and LPG tankers and the vast orderbook for the offshore sector. With a conservative 70%/30% debt to debt to equity financing structure, the implication is that tanker owners will need to tap into the markets for nearly $80 billion.

children.title: Cash or Credit?
children.summary: The tie between shipping and the investment community, and Wall Street in particular, has been growing stronger for the past several years. The coming months and years will be a test of this bond.
